title: Early Atmosphere, Oceans and Life on Earth
seo_title: Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science: Atmosphere, Hydrosphere and Biosphere Worksheets
standard_code: Earth and Environmental Science Unit 1: Development of the atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere
standard_text: Outgassing and the early atmosphere and oceans; the origin of life; stromatolites, cyanobacteria and the Great Oxidation Event; banded iron formations and the ozone layer; the fossil record and mass extinctions; coevolution of life and Earth. (Senior Secondary Earth and Environmental Science, Unit 1: Introduction to Earth systems)
meta_desc: Free Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science worksheets on Earth's early atmosphere, oceans and life: stromatolites, the Great Oxidation Event, banded iron formations, Ediacaran fossils and mass extinctions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Life changed Earth, and Earth changed life.
key_sub: Cyanobacteria → oxygen → banded iron, ozone and complex life.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth's first atmosphere came from volcanic outgassing (CO₂, water vapour, N₂) with almost no oxygen. As Earth cooled, water condensed into oceans.

Cyanobacteria built stromatolites (3.5 billion years old in the Pilbara; living ones at Shark Bay). Their oxygen first reacted with dissolved iron, forming banded iron formations, then built up in the air in the Great Oxidation Event about 2.4 billion years ago, allowing ozone and complex life. The Ediacaran fossils of South Australia are among the first animals.

Example

Which came first: banded iron formations or the build-up of oxygen in air?

oxygen first reacted with iron in the oceans

only then did it build up in the atmosphere

Answer: banded iron formations

Example

Order: Earth forms, first life, Great Oxidation, Ediacaran animals

4.54 Ga, ~3.5 Ga, ~2.4 Ga, ~0.56 Ga

Answer: in that order

Common mistakes

  • Thinking early Earth's air was like today's.
  • Saying stromatolites are plants: they are built by cyanobacteria.
  • Thinking life appeared only after the dinosaurs: microbes existed for billions of years before.

faq.q: What evidence shows when oxygen built up in the atmosphere?
faq.a: Banded iron formations stop forming, red beds (rusted land sediments) appear, and some minerals that cannot survive with oxygen disappear from rocks after about 2.4 billion years ago.

faq.q: Why is Australia important for studying early life?
faq.a: It has some of the oldest fossils on Earth: 3.5-billion-year-old stromatolites in the Pilbara, living stromatolites at Shark Bay and Ediacaran animals in the Flinders Ranges.

sets.title: A timeline of Earth and life

items.q: Which came first: the Great Oxidation Event, or the first animals?
c: They happened at the same time.
items.e: The Great Oxidation Event: about 2.4 billion years ago; the first animals: about 0.6 billion years ago.

items.q: What is the leading explanation for the extinction of the dinosaurs 66 million years ago?
c: an ice age caused by Earth's orbit only
a large asteroid impact, together with major volcanic eruptions
a change in Earth's magnetic field
items.e: The Chicxulub crater is evidence of the impact.

items.q: What is coevolution of life and Earth?
c: life and Earth never affect each other
life changes Earth's systems, and those changes in turn affect how life evolves
items.e: Oxygen from life allowed animals to evolve.

items.q: Which came first: the first forests, or the first oxygen-making cyanobacteria?
c: They happened at the same time.
items.e: The first oxygen-making cyanobacteria: about 2.7 billion years ago; the first forests: about 0.38 billion years ago.

items.q: What is a mass extinction?

the loss of a large proportion of species in a geologically short time
items.e: There have been five major mass extinctions.
